name: Gyalsumdo-Nubri

tone_statements.citation: Donohue, Cathryn. 2022. Changing identity and linguistic practices in Nubri. In Roche & Hyslop (eds.), Bordering Tibetan Languages, ch. 7. Amsterdam University Press.
tone_statements.quote: Pitch-melody: Four Gyalsumdo speakers (5 measurement points) … The four categories are not obvious, but when WT 1/2 and WT 3/4 are merged into a proposed “high” v. “low”, the di#erences are signi!cant … Gyalsumdo … Summary … My Proposal … Characterized by … “Hi” (WT 1/2) … Higher F0 (no evidence for contour diffs. yet), ±asp obs. … “Low” (WT 3/4) … Lower F0, tendency towards obstruent voicing, particularly by males, weak evidence for shorter vocal fold closure for vowels, obstruent aspiration rare
tone_statements.locator: Slide 21 'Observations & Analysis: Pitch-melody' and slide 32 'Summary: Gyalsumdo' two-column table read row-wise; no page numbers
tone_statements.summary: Tentative instrumental proposal: two registers, high (Written Tibetan classes 1/2) vs low (3/4), separated by F0, obstruent voicing/breathiness in the low; no contour contrast yet; stress not treated.

tone_statements.citation: Donohue, Cathryn. 2021. Tonal morphology in Sama Nubri: Case marking and transitivity alternations. Studies in Language 45(2): 408-427.
tone_statements.quote: Nubri has five contrasting tones. These have distinct contours on monosyllables, and a set of corresponding contrasts on polysyllables (Donohue & Donohue 2019). … Table 1. Nubri tonal contrasts. Description Feature Tone letters … High H 44 [ɲiŋ44~45] nyīng ‘heart’ High fall HL 53 [t̪ ɐ53~52] tà ‘horse’ Mid Ø (M) 33 [mi33~332] mi ‘person’ Low fall L 21 [ɲa21] nyǎ ‘fish Low convex LHL 231 [t̪ o̤231~232] dô ‘potato’ … The mid tone is represented as tone-less, which is phonetically realized as a mid tone. In Nubri, five tonal contrasts are maintained in polysyllabic words
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2 'Tone in Nubri', Table 1, manuscript pp. 2-3; downstepped H (OCP) sec. 3 ms pp. 7-9; floating H ms pp. 13, 15
tone_statements.summary: Five contrastive tones: high 44, high fall 53, mid 33 (toneless), low fall 21, low convex 231, low ones breathy; same five on disyllables; floating H marks genitive/transitivity; H+H gives downstep.

sources.citation: Tournadre, Nicolas & Hiroyuki Suzuki. 2023. The Tibetic Languages: An Introduction to the Family of Languages Derived from Old Tibetan. Paris: LACITO. Sec. 7.3.3 'Stress' (pp. 241-242), 7.3.4 'Prosodic patterns' (pp. 242-243), p. 576 n. 51
sources.note: Family-level only: 'The distinction of stress is attested mainly in Balti'; tonal dialects have a trochaic (strong-weak) pattern on the first two syllables. Nubri and Gyalsumdo appear only in the Kyirong-Yolmo classification (p. 576 with n. 51 citing Hildebrandt & Perry 2011); no Nubri- or Gyalsumdo-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page nubr1241 (Gyalsumdo-Nubri); dialects Gyalsumdo [gyal1236], Nubri [nubr1243] with Lho, Namrung, Prok, Sama [sama1294]
sources.note: Bibliographic only; lists Hildebrandt & Perry 2011 for subclassification.

sources.citation: Hildebrandt, Kristine A. & J. Joseph Perry. 2011. Preliminary notes on Gyalsumdo, an undocumented Tibetan variety in Manang District, Nepal. Himalayan Linguistics 10(1): 167-185. DOI 10.5070/H910123573
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Sec. 4 (pp. 172-178) is an acoustic study of the reflexes of the four Central Tibetan tone/register series in 50 obstruent-initial words from one speaker; p. 174 states measurements used only the initial syllable 'under the assumption that more patterns and contrasts are located on the initial syllable of disyllabics', as in Kyirong (Huber 2002). Appendix marks perceived relative pitch (ā high, a low), not stress.

sources.citation: Donohue, Cathryn & Mark Donohue. 2023. The vowels of Nubri from the perspective of other Tibetan languages. Nepalese Linguistics 37(1): 10-18. DOI 10.3126/nl.v37i1.60008
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Nine oral vowels plus contrastive nasalisation on three; length, breathiness and creak treated as functions of the tonal contrasts.

sources.citation: Dhakal, Dubi Nanda. 2022. Finite verb forms in Nubri with a focus on conjunct-disjunct distinction. Nepalese Linguistics 35: 41-49. DOI 10.3126/nl.v35i01.46558
Dhakal, Dubi Nanda. 2019. Nouns and noun phrase structure in Nubri. Gipan 4: 38-53. DOI 10.3126/gipan.v4i0.35455 (Glottolog study of one feature ref)
Donohue, Cathryn & Mark Donohue. 2019. The complexity of tone in Nubri. Nepalese Linguistics 34: 18-25. DOI 10.3126/nl.v34i1.41161
sources.note: Silent on stress (the word occurs only in the title of the cited Caplow 2009 dissertation). Describes Sama(gaun) Nubri as having five contrastive tones on monosyllables (H 44, HM 53, M 33, ML 21, LML 231; low tones breathy) and the same five contrasts preserved on disyllables, with restricted tonal combinations.
